facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta is a genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived between 69 and 66 million years ago in the Naashoibito member of the Ojo Alamo Formation.
facts.quote: Glyptodontopelta (meaning "Glyptodon shield") is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (lower to upper Maastrichtian, 69 to 66 Ma) in what is now the Naashoibito member of the Ojo Alamo Formation.

facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta was named in 2000 by Tracy Ford.
facts.quote: It was named in 2000 by Tracy Ford.

facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta was considered a dubious name in a 2004 review, but a 2008 publication by Michael Burns argued that its distinctive armor made it a valid genus.
facts.quote: It was concluded to be a dubious name, a nomen dubium, in a 2004 review of the Ankylosauria, but a 2008 publication by Michael Burns concurred with Ford that its armor was distinctive enough to consider it valid.

facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta mimus lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian, approximately 71 to 65 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Glyptodontopelta mimus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Glyptodontopelta (gr. "escudo de Glyptodon") de dinosaurio tireóforo anquilosauriano, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 71 y 65 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta was an armored dinosaur approximately 5 meters long, 2 meters high, and weighing 2800 kilograms.
facts.quote: Glyptodontopelta fue un dinosaurio acorazado de alrededor de 5 metros de largo 2 de alto y un peso de 2800 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The name Glyptodontopelta comes from its pelvic armor, which has a shape similar to that of the extinct mammal glyptodon.
facts.quote: Su nombre proviene de su blindaje pélvico que posee una forma un similar al del mamífero extinto gliptodonte.

facts.statement: The armor consists of large, asymmetric shields that are hexagonal, pentagonal, or quadrilateral with low or flat peaks arranged in a mosaic pattern to form a solid shield over the ilia, with small ossicles filling the gaps.
facts.quote: La armadura consiste en escudos grandes y asimétricos, hexagonales, pentagonales y cuadriláteros que tienen picos bajos o planos que se bordean y se fijan en un modelo del mosaico, formando un blindaje sólido sobre los iliones, entre los cuales hay pequeños osículos ocupando todos los lugares disponibles.

facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta fossils were found in the Naashoibito member of the Kirtland shale at Barrel Springs Creek in San Juan County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: Glyptodontopelta se encontró en miembro Naashoibito de la pizarra de Kirtland, en el arroyo Barrel Springs, condado de San Juan, Nuevo México.

facts.statement: Gilmore published Glyptodontopelta as an indeterminate genus and species in 1919 based only on parts of the armor.
facts.quote: Gilmore en 1919, lo publicó como género y especie indeterminada, basado solo en partes de la armadura.

facts.statement: Lehman classified Glyptodontopelta as a nodosaurid in 1981.
facts.quote: Lehman en 1981 lo clasifica como un nodosáurido.

facts.statement: Tracy Ford described Glyptodontopelta in 2000 in the Bulletin of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science, number 17, on pages 171.
facts.quote: En el 2000 Tracy Ford lo describió en el Boletín del Museo de Historia Natural y Ciencia de Nuevo México n.º 17, en las páginas 171.

facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta mimus has been placed in the subfamily Stegopeltinae with Stegopelta, but other researchers include it within Shamosaurinae.
facts.quote: Glyptodontopelta mimus es colocado junto con Stegopelta en una nueva subfamilia llamada Stegopeltinae, pero otros lo incluyen dentro de Shamosaurinae.

facts.statement: Michael Burns classified Glyptodontopelta as a Nodosauridae and proposed that the New Mexico taxon Edmontonia australis is a synonym of Glyptodontopelta mimus.
facts.quote: Burns también lo consideró un Nodosauridae y se propuso que otro taxón basado en armadura de Nuevo México, Edmontonia australis, es un sinónimo de Glyptodontopelta mimus.

facts.statement: Glyptodontopelta belongs to the family Nodosauridae.
Glyptodontopelta is classified in the class Ornithischia.
Glyptodontopelta lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the classification of Glyptodontopelta, with Michael Burns rejecting Tracy Ford's placement in Stegopeltinae and assigning it to Nodosauridae instead.
facts.quote: Burns also assigned Glyptodontopelta to Nodosauridae — rejecting Ford's Stegopeltinae
